 Waiver Granted Pursuant to Section 39
 In accordance with section 39 of the Conflict of Interest Act, Ms. Scieur-Aparicio, former Director of Communications in the Office of the Minister of National Revenue, has been granted a reduction of her limitation period under section 36 to permit her to accept employment with Affaires Politiques, a public relations firm. 
Ms. Scieur-Aparicio applied for a reduction of the period that applies to former reporting public office holders for one year following their last day in office. The reduction allows Ms. Scieur-Aparicio to accept a employment with Affaires Politiques. In reviewing Ms. Scieur-Aparicio’s request, I considered all relevant factors listed under subsection 39(3) of the Act, which include the following: 
- Circumstances of departure: Ms. Scieur-Aparicio departed public office after less than two months.
- General employment prospects: Ms. Scieur-Aparicio’s employment prospects are limited given her expertise and region of residence.
- Degree to which the new employer might gain unfair commercial advantage: No unfair advantage is envisaged since the duration in the position was very short and Ms. Scieur-Aparicio had no influence on the development of policies.
In light of the above, I have determined that the public interest in granting the reduction in relation to Ms. Scieur-Aparicio’s employment with Affaires Politiques outweighs the public interest in maintaining the prohibition. I have therefore waived the limitation period. 
All other post‐employment obligations under the Act continue to apply, including the prohibition on contracting or accepting employment or an appointment to a board position with any other entity set out in subsection 35(1) as well as the prohibition on making representations within the meaning of subsection 35(2), for the duration of Ms. Scieur-Aparicio’s limitation period.
